learning_goal: Place the thalamus by its six walls rather than by memorising a picture — third ventricle medially, internal capsule laterally, hypothalamus below the hypothalamic sulcus, fornix and ventricular body above — then use that position to explain why every sensory modality except smell stops here, and why a lesion a centimetre across produces a whole-body sensory loss that later turns to pain.

structures.name: right thalamus
structures.label: Thalamus (R)
structures.narration: An egg of grey matter about four centimetres long lying obliquely at the very centre of the hemisphere, its narrow anterior tubercle pointing forwards and medially and its swollen pulvinar overhanging the midbrain behind. This is one undivided mesh: the internal medullary lamina and the twenty-odd nuclei it separates are named in beat 5 and are not drawn, so every nucleus you hear about is a region of this single shape rather than an object you can click. Four points ON that shape are marked, because they could be measured against neighbouring meshes rather than guessed: the two geniculate bodies, the anterior tubercle and the posterior pole.

structures.name: left thalamus
structures.label: Thalamus (L)
structures.narration: The left thalamus. Both are shown because the pair defines the third ventricle between them, and because in most brains the two touch across that slit at the interthalamic adhesion — a grey contact, not a commissure, carrying no fibres from one side to the other. The adhesion is not a separate mesh, so on screen the two shapes simply approach each other.

structures.name: right stria medullaris of thalamus
structures.label: Stria medullaris (R)
structures.narration: The white ridge along the upper medial edge of the right thalamus. It is the ridge that marks where the medial (ventricular) surface meets the superior surface, and it is a useful border for that alone; the fibres running in it are heading backwards to the habenula. Do not confuse it with the stria terminalis, which is a different bundle following the tail of the caudate.

structures.name: left stria medullaris of thalamus
structures.label: Stria medullaris (L)
structures.narration: The same ridge on the left, converging with its fellow on the habenula behind.

structures.name: habenula
structures.label: Habenula
structures.narration: Where the two striae medullares end, at the posterior end of the roof of the third ventricle. Habenula, stria medullaris and pineal together are the epithalamus — dorsal and posterior to the thalamus proper and, despite the shared name, not part of it. Shown as context so the posterior boundary of the thalamus is a shape rather than an assertion.

structures.name: pineal body
structures.label: Pineal body
structures.narration: The midline cone slung backwards from the epithalamus between the two thalami, sitting immediately above the superior colliculi. It calcifies with age, which makes it the midline marker radiologists use to see whether a mass has shifted the brain sideways. A pineal tumour presses on the tectum below it and on the cerebral aqueduct, which is why it presents with an upgaze palsy and a hydrocephalus rather than with anything endocrine.

structures.name: third ventricle
structures.label: Third ventricle
structures.narration: The midline slit the two thalami face across. The medial surface of the thalamus is literally the upper part of the lateral wall of this ventricle, and a shallow groove on that wall — the hypothalamic sulcus, running from the interventricular foramen to the cerebral aqueduct — is the line below which the wall stops being thalamus and becomes hypothalamus. The sulcus is a surface groove with no mesh of its own, so it is described here and not drawn.

structures.name: right lateral ventricle
structures.label: Lateral ventricle (R)
structures.narration: The superior surface of the thalamus forms most of the floor of the body of this ventricle, so anything growing off the thalamus grows straight into CSF. Ghosted here so the roof of the thalamus reads as a floor of something else.

structures.name: left lateral ventricle
structures.label: Lateral ventricle (L)
structures.narration: The left cavity, ghosted for the same reason.

structures.name: right fornix of forebrain
structures.label: Fornix (R)
structures.narration: The white arch that rides over the top of the thalamus in the midline and then dives down in front of it as the column of the fornix, ending in the mammillary body. Its column and the anterior tubercle of the thalamus together bound the interventricular foramen — the surgeon's landmark for finding the thalamus from inside the ventricle.

structures.name: left fornix of forebrain
structures.label: Fornix (L)
structures.narration: The left arch, the mirror of the right, ending in the same way on the mammillary body of its own side.

structures.name: anterior limb of right internal capsule
structures.label: Internal capsule — anterior limb (R)
structures.narration: The lateral wall of the thalamus is the internal capsule — but it is the POSTERIOR limb that lies against the thalamus, and only the anterior limb exists as a mesh in this catalog. What is drawn here is therefore in front of the thalamus rather than beside it, and beat 3 says so at the point where the difference matters. Read the drawn sheet as the near end of a sheet that continues backwards past the thalamus and is not shown.

structures.name: anterior limb of left internal capsule
structures.label: Internal capsule — anterior limb (L)
structures.narration: The left anterior limb, carrying the same caveat: the limb that actually walls the thalamus laterally is the posterior one, which has no mesh.

structures.name: right putamen
structures.label: Putamen (R)
structures.narration: Context, and the far side of the wall: on an axial cut the posterior limb of the capsule runs between the thalamus medially and the lentiform nucleus laterally. Basal ganglia rather than diencephalon, and taught in their own scene.

structures.name: right caudate nucleus
structures.label: Caudate nucleus (R)
structures.narration: The body of the caudate arches over the superolateral edge of the thalamus in the floor of the ventricular body, separated from it by a groove carrying the stria terminalis and the thalamostriate vein. That groove is the boundary between diencephalon and telencephalon on this surface, and it is the line a surgeon opens along.

structures.name: mammillary body
structures.label: Mammillary body
structures.narration: Hypothalamus, not thalamus — shown to make the floor of the diencephalon visible and to mark where the fornix ends. From here the mammillothalamic tract runs up into the anterior nucleus of the thalamus, which is the step of the Papez circuit that makes an anterior thalamic lesion a memory lesion. That tract has no mesh; the two ends of it do. Note this single mesh stands for both mammillary bodies — the catalog carries no left and right.

structures.name: right optic tract
structures.label: Optic tract (R)
structures.narration: The visual afferent, sweeping round the cerebral peduncle to end on the lateral geniculate body — a knuckle on the underside of the pulvinar. The geniculate bodies are thalamus, and this is the clearest demonstration of what the thalamus is for: the visual pathway does not reach cortex without stopping here. The geniculate bodies have no mesh on disk — they are in the catalog and have not been fetched — but the point where this tract meets the thalamus was measured at audit and is marked: the tract is drawn arriving at that marker rather than at an unnamed stretch of thalamic surface.

structures.name: left optic tract
structures.label: Optic tract (L)
structures.narration: The left tract, ending on the left lateral geniculate body in the same way.

structures.name: brachium of right inferior colliculus
structures.label: Brachium of inferior colliculus (R)
structures.narration: The auditory equivalent, and the reason it is worth having on screen: it runs forwards from the inferior colliculus of the midbrain up onto the medial geniculate body. Hearing takes the same architecture as vision — a midbrain relay, then a thalamic relay, then cortex — and the two brachia are the visible proof that the geniculate bodies belong to the thalamus and not to the tectum. The medial geniculate body is not on disk either; the point where this brachium lands on the thalamus was measured at audit and is marked.

structures.name: right inferior colliculus
structures.label: Inferior colliculus (R)
structures.narration: Midbrain tectum, below and behind the pulvinar — the far end of the brachium. Context only; the brainstem scenes teach it.

structures.name: right superior colliculus
structures.label: Superior colliculus (R)
structures.narration: The visual reflex centre of the tectum, tucked under the overhang of the pulvinar and under the pineal. It is here to show how little room there is behind the thalamus: a pineal or a posterior thalamic mass reaches this plate almost immediately, and the upgaze palsy follows.

structures.label: Lateral geniculate body (R)
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: CONTACT patch between the right thalamus (FMA258714) and the right optic tract (FMA62382), averaged over the 55 parent vertices within 3 mm of the tract — gap 0.45 mm, patch centroid 0.43 mm off the surface. One witness, because the optic tract is the only mesh that reaches this knuckle; the check on it is the medial geniculate anchor derived the same way in the same run, which lands at u 0.53 against this one's u 0.20 — that is, the lateral geniculate is measurably LATERAL to the medial geniculate on a right-sided mesh where lower u is more lateral. Both sit at w 0.04-0.06, the inferior surface, which is where the geniculate bodies belong.
structures.narration: The knuckle on the underside of the pulvinar where the optic tract ends. It is thalamus, not midbrain, and it is the relay the visual pathway cannot bypass: retina to optic tract to here, then optic radiation to the occipital cortex. No mesh for it has been delivered — FMA73303 exists in the catalog and is not in meshes-lite/ — so this marker is the measured patch where the tract meets the thalamic surface: it shows you where the body is, not its extent, and it should be replaced by the real mesh once that is fetched.

structures.label: Medial geniculate body (R)
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: CONTACT patch between the right thalamus (FMA258714) and the brachium of the right inferior colliculus (FMA73463), averaged over the 18 parent vertices within 3 mm — gap 0.13 mm. Weaker than the lateral geniculate anchor and the weakness is recorded rather than smoothed over: the patch is 18 vertices and its centroid sits 1.45 mm off the surface, against 55 vertices and 0.43 mm for the lateral. One witness. The cross-check is positional and it passes: this anchor is medial (u 0.53) to the lateral geniculate (u 0.20) on a right-sided mesh, and both are on the inferior surface.
structures.narration: Where the brachium of the inferior colliculus lands. Auditory relay, medial to its visual counterpart, and the second half of the proof that the geniculate bodies are thalamic: both brachia climb forwards out of the tectum ONTO the thalamus rather than staying in the midbrain.

structures.label: Anterior tubercle (R)
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: EXTREME -y on the right thalamus (FMA258714) — the most anterior vertex of the mesh, 18.9 mm from the centroid. Verified anterior with the mesh centroids rather than assumed: pineal body y=-75.3, mammillary body y=-103.3, so more negative y is anterior on these meshes and +z is superior. Stable under --slab z:0.4,1.0 and z:0.5,1.0 (identical vertex) and moves 1.5 mm under z:0.6,1.0. The result lands anteromedial (u 0.67, where higher u is medial on a right-sided mesh) and in the upper half (w 0.56), which is where the anterior tubercle is.
structures.narration: The forward point of the thalamus, and half of a surgical landmark: with the column of the fornix in front of it, it bounds the interventricular foramen. If you are inside the body of the lateral ventricle looking for the thalamus, this is the corner you find first.

structures.label: Posterior pole — pulvinar overhang (R)
structures.calibrated_by: geometry: EXTREME +y on the right thalamus (FMA258714), 17.2 mm from the centroid, with +y confirmed posterior from the pineal and mammillary centroids as above. READ THE LABEL EXACTLY: the pulvinar is a REGION of the posterior thalamus, not a point, and no point definition can bound a region. What is measured here is the posterior extremity of the mesh — the tip of the overhang — and the label says pole rather than pulvinar for that reason. It lands posterolateral (u 0.32) and low (w 0.28), consistent with an overhang that leans out over the tectum.
structures.narration: The back end of the thalamus, overhanging the midbrain tectum. This marks the tip of the overhang, not the whole pulvinar. It is worth having on screen because of how little space is behind it: the superior colliculus is immediately below and the pineal immediately medial, which is why a posterior thalamic or pineal mass produces an upgaze palsy so early.

views.title: The centre of the hemisphere
views.narration: Two grey eggs set obliquely at the centre of the brain with a slit between them. Each is about four centimetres long, narrow and pointed in front, broad and overhanging behind. Everything else in this scene is a wall: the slit between them is the third ventricle, the arch above is the fornix, the cavity above that is the body of the lateral ventricle. Fix the shape and the obliquity now — the anterior ends nearly meet in the midline while the posterior ends splay apart over the midbrain — because every later beat is about what lies against which surface.

views.title: Six walls, and the sulcus that sets the lower one
views.narration: Name the neighbours in order and the thalamus stops needing to be memorised. Medially, the third ventricle — the thalamic surface IS the upper half of its lateral wall. Above, the floor of the body of the lateral ventricle, with the fornix arching over medially and the body of the caudate riding the lateral edge. Laterally, the internal capsule. Below, the hypothalamus and the subthalamus. Behind, the pulvinar overhangs the midbrain tectum. The one boundary you cannot see is the one that is asked about: the hypothalamic sulcus, a shallow groove on the ventricular wall running from the interventricular foramen back to the cerebral aqueduct. Above that line the wall is thalamus, below it hypothalamus. It is a groove on a surface and has no mesh here, so trace it between its two ends: the interventricular foramen in front, which IS drawn here — bounded by the column of the fornix and the anterior tubercle — and the cerebral aqueduct behind, which is NOT in this scene and is described rather than shown. Only the front end is something you can look at. The anterior tubercle is marked here, and the posterior pole with it, so the forward-and-medial tilt of the egg reads as a line between two measured points rather than as an impression.

views.title: The axial cut — and what is missing from it
views.narration: This is the cut every CT head is read on. Medial to lateral it goes: third ventricle, thalamus, posterior limb of the internal capsule, lentiform nucleus, insula. Two of those five are lit — the thalamus and the lentiform nucleus — and the sheet that should lie between them is the one this catalog does not carry. Only the anterior limb of the capsule exists as a mesh, and the anterior limb lies in front of the thalamus, between caudate head and lentiform nucleus, not beside it. So read the gap between the two lit shapes as the posterior limb: it carries the corticospinal fibres for the opposite half of the body and the thalamocortical fibres coming out of the thalamus itself, which is why a bleed that starts in the thalamus becomes a hemiplegia the moment it crosses one centimetre laterally.

views.title: The coronal cut — roof, floor and the pair across the midline
views.narration: On the coronal cut the diencephalon stacks vertically and the stack is the answer to most exam questions here. Fornix at the top, thalamus below it on each side of the ventricular slit, hypothalamus below the sulcus with the mammillary body marking its back end, and the whole column suspended between the two lentiform nuclei. Note what does not happen across the midline: the two thalami touch at the interthalamic adhesion in about three quarters of brains, but nothing crosses there. It is grey matter in contact, not a commissure — the epithalamic commissures behind, at the habenula and under the pineal, are the ones that do carry fibres.

views.title: Everything stops here except smell
views.narration: Two afferents are traced arriving, and they are the two you can see, each ending on a marked point: the optic tract onto the lateral geniculate body, and the brachium of the inferior colliculus onto the medial geniculate body. Those two markers are measured contact patches, not drawn nuclei — they tell you where each body is, not how big it is, and the lateral one sitting lateral to the medial one is the relation worth taking away. Take them as the pattern for the rest, which are described only. Body sensation from the medial lemniscus and the spinothalamic tract lands in the ventral posterolateral nucleus, the face in the ventral posteromedial; the cerebellum and the globus pallidus feed the ventral lateral and ventral anterior nuclei and so shape movement; the mammillothalamic tract feeds the anterior nucleus and so serves memory; the medial dorsal nucleus talks to prefrontal cortex; the pulvinar to the parietal and occipital association cortex. Olfaction is the exception in the whole nervous system — it reaches cortex directly and only afterwards involves the medial dorsal nucleus. None of those nuclei is a mesh: this is one undivided shape, divided in life by a Y-shaped sheet of white matter called the internal medullary lamina, and nothing in this scene draws that sheet or the nuclei on either side of it.

views.title: Small lesion, whole half of the body
views.narration: Because every modality funnels through a structure the size of a walnut, a lacunar infarct here produces a pure sensory stroke: numbness of the opposite face, arm, trunk and leg at once, with no weakness and no cortical signs, from a lesion in the ventral posterior nucleus a few millimetres across. Weeks to months later a proportion of these turn into the thalamic pain syndrome of Dejerine and Roussy — the numb side becomes spontaneously and unbearably painful, and light touch is agony. A larger thalamic haemorrhage adds two signs worth knowing because they are almost specific: the eyes deviate down and inwards, looking at the patient's own nose, from pressure on the tectum below, and the hand takes up a posture with the wrist flexed and the fingers extended. The arterial supply is not drawn — no cerebral artery of any kind exists in this catalog — but the single fact worth carrying is that in some people both anteromedial thalami are fed by one vessel off one posterior cerebral artery, the artery of Percheron, so one occlusion infarcts both thalami and the patient presents with a sudden loss of consciousness and amnesia rather than with a hemi-anything.

gaps: THE THALAMUS IS ONE UNDIVIDED MESH. FMA258714 / FMA258716 carry no nuclei and no internal medullary lamina. Searched nucleus, nuclei, lamina, medullary, pulvinar, geniculate, ventral posterior, VPL, VPM, anterior nucleus, medial dorsal, reticular, intralaminar, centromedian — the only 'nucleus' entries in the whole catalog are the two caudate nuclei. Every nucleus named in beat 5 is therefore described and not shown, and beat 5 says so in itself. CORRECTED 2026-09-08: `geniculate` was listed among the searched strings above, and it DOES return four entries — FMA73303 / FMA73304 lateral and FMA73309 / FMA73310 medial. None of the four is in meshes-lite/, so nothing on screen changes and the anchors below remain the right treatment for today, but the reason is DELIVERY and not absence: this is a fetch job with four known ids, and when they arrive the two geniculate anchors should be retired in favour of the meshes. The lateral and medial geniculate bodies matter most, because the two afferents that ARE traced end on them; AS OF THE 2026-09-04 AUDIT BOTH ARE MARKED AS MEASURED ANCHORS on the thalamic surface rather than left as unnamed stretches of it — lateral geniculate from the optic-tract contact (0.45 mm, 55-vertex patch), medial geniculate from the brachium of the inferior colliculus (0.13 mm, 18-vertex patch), each cross-checked against the other for mediolateral order. They are still not nuclei: an anchor marks where a body is and says nothing about its extent, and the two structure cards and both anchor cards say so.

NO POSTERIOR LIMB OF THE INTERNAL CAPSULE, so the lateral wall of the thalamus is absent. Searched capsule, limb, genu, retrolentiform, sublentiform, corona, radiata, thalamic radiation, corticospinal, pyramidal, lemniscus, spinothalamic, tract. Only the anterior limb exists (FMA72908 / FMA72909) and it lies in FRONT of the thalamus, not beside it — the structure cards for both limbs and beat 3 state this explicitly rather than letting the drawn sheet be read as the wall. This is the same absence recorded in the basal ganglia scene of this topic and the two files state it the same way.

NO INTERTHALAMIC ADHESION, NO HYPOTHALAMIC SULCUS. Searched adhesion, massa intermedia, interthalamic, commissure (which returns anterior, posterior and fornical commissures only), sulcus, hypothalamic. Both are named in beats 2 and 4 as features of surfaces that are drawn, and both are the sort of thing that would be authored as an anchor if the parent meshes were fetched — the sulcus in particular is a line rather than a point and would need a run of anchors, so it is described between two landmarks that do exist, the interventricular foramen and the cerebral aqueduct.

NO MAMMILLOTHALAMIC TRACT and no tract of any kind. Both ends exist — the mammillary body (FMA74877) and the thalamus — and the connection between them is stated in the mammillary body card and in beat 5 as a described pathway. Searched mammillothalamic, mamillothalamic, tract, bundle, fasciculus, lemniscus, Vicq d'Azyr.

THE MAMMILLARY BODY IS A SINGLE UNPAIRED MESH. FMA74877 is 'mammillary body' with no left or right in the catalog, although the structure is a pair in life. Its card says so. The same mesh and the same caveat appear in the hypothalamus and pituitary scene of this topic, worded consistently.

NO SUBTHALAMUS. The subthalamic region is named in beat 2 as the fourth wall below and is not drawn; there is no subthalamic nucleus, no zona incerta and no substantia nigra in the catalog (searched subthalam, Luys, zona incerta, nigra, substantia). Recorded identically in the basal ganglia scene.

NO INTRACRANIAL VESSEL OF ANY KIND, so the artery of Percheron and the thalamoperforating branches of beat 6 are named and not drawn. Searched Percheron, perforat, thalamoperforat, posterior cerebral, communicating, choroidal, basilar, Willis, cerebral artery, dural sinus, thalamostriate vein, internal cerebral vein. This matches the neuroanatomy blood-supply routing recorded across this course: the catalog holds no cerebral artery, no circle of Willis and no dural venous sinus. The thalamostriate vein is named in the caudate card as the content of the groove and is likewise not drawn.

SIDES, STATED EXPLICITLY BECAUSE THE IDS DO NOT CARRY THEM. Right / left in this scene: thalamus FMA258714 right and FMA258716 left — NOT consecutive, and the trap in this topic; stria medullaris of thalamus FMA73413 right and FMA73414 left; anterior limb of internal capsule FMA72908 right and FMA72909 left; lateral ventricle FMA78449 right and FMA78450 left; fornix of forebrain FMA72924 right and FMA72925 left. The optic tracts break the pattern entirely and were the second trap: right is FMA62382 and left is FMA67936, from different id ranges. FOUR ANCHORS WERE DERIVED AT THE 2026-09-04 AUDIT, and two features were refused. This note previously said no anchors were authored and named the work as open; it was done. MEASURED: lateral geniculate body, --parent FMA258714 --contact FMA62382 --area 3, gap 0.45 mm over 55 vertices; medial geniculate body, --contact FMA73463 --area 3, gap 0.13 mm over 18 vertices; anterior tubercle, --extreme -y, 18.9 mm from the centroid and identical under --slab z:0.4,1.0 and z:0.5,1.0; posterior pole, --extreme +y, 17.2 mm from the centroid. All four are status needs-review: measuring proves the coordinate, only looking proves it landed. TWO CHECKS THAT MADE THEM TRUSTWORTHY, both worth repeating elsewhere. First, the axis was confirmed from mesh centroids rather than from the tool's report: derive-landmark.mjs calls the thalamus's long axis y, and it is right here, but the DIRECTION of y had to be settled independently — pineal body y=-75.3 against mammillary body y=-103.3 proves more negative y is anterior, and z=1560 for the thalamus against z=1551 for the pineal proves +z is superior. Without that, --extreme -y would have returned a measured, reproducible and completely wrong 'posterior pole'. This is the same trap the spleen scene recorded on 2026-08-29 and it recurs on brain meshes. Second, the geniculate anchors check each other: one witness each is one witness too few, but on a right-sided mesh lower u is more lateral, and the lateral geniculate came out at u 0.20 against the medial's u 0.53, with both at w 0.04-0.06 on the inferior surface. The anatomy predicted that ordering and the measurement produced it. REFUSED, and the refusals are definition problems, not delivery ones: the HYPOTHALAMIC SULCUS is a line on a surface, and a line needs a run of anchors that this tool has no primitive for — a single point on it would be arbitrary and would be believed. The PULVINAR is a region, so no point definition bounds it; what was measured is the posterior extremity of the mesh and it is labelled 'posterior pole' for exactly that reason, with the distinction stated in its own calibrated_by. The groove holding the stria terminalis is likewise a line, between the thalamus and the caudate, and was not attempted.

INTERNAL CAPSULE, BASAL GANGLIA AND HYPOTHALAMUS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT IN covers[]. All three are separate CURRICULUM.json structures, two of them in this same topic, and each appears here only as far as the thalamus needs it — the capsule as the lateral wall, the caudate and putamen as what lies beyond it, the hypothalamus and mammillary body as the floor. Claiming any of them would hide a gap that is currently visible.

THE POSTERIOR END OF THE HYPOTHALAMIC SULCUS IS DESCRIBED, NOT SHOWN. The cerebral aqueduct exists in the catalog as FMA78467 but is not a structure in this scene, so beat 2 has one drawn landmark and one spoken one.
